catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is phonemic, it for example differentiates future and near past tense forms of verbs. The stress is not written.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim on p. 3 of the OPD PDF we hold. (2) The classification rests on a 4-page SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (2004 print of Stefaniw's 1990 mss; REAP labels it an unreviewed draft): two sentences, no data. For this language that is nonetheless close to the best that exists: Glottolog's genuine descriptive bibliography reduces to Stefaniw 1987 (48 pp. ms.) plus this OPD; OLAC, the SIL archive and CrossRef show no phonology article, thesis or dictionary. (3) Independent support comes from a file we already hold for the sister languoid: Blowers 1970 (PL A-26) states that the Auwa dialect north of Ialibu (= Glottolog's Aua dialect of Imbongu) has the same phonemic system as Kaugel, where 'stress is phonemic.. often the only difference in words to change meaning' and unpredictable outside verbs — consistent with lexical. sources.quote: p. 1: 'A brief study was also made of the Auwa dialect spoken north of Ialibu. Though the verb endings are considerably different in Auwa, yet sentence structure, general grammatical features, and phonemic sounds are the same as herein described.' (Auwa/Aua = the dialect Glottolog files under imbo1238.) p. 5: 'In the Kaugel dialect, stress is phonemic, it being often the only difference in words to change meaning. Stress can be predicted quite accurately in verb forms but not in other words.'
sources.locator: sec. II 'Background' (p. 1) and sec. III.B 'Suprasegmental Phonemes' (p. 5)

sources.quote: Bibliographic only: the SIL archive holds exactly two linguistic items on Imbongu — Stefaniw 1987 'A comparison of Imbongu grammar with the Kaugel grammar essentials' (ms., archives/43852) and 'Imbongu Organised Phonology Data' (2011 posting, 4 pp., phonological description, draft). Everything else is Pence 1964 (mis-tagged), kinship, and Bible-translation papers.
